name: Korean Demilitarized Zone
blurb: A fenced-off strip where cranes, water deer and gorals found sanctuary.

tip.title: Remove the rice fields
tip.text: Cranes, geese and boar lean on rice gleanings in winter. Remove Rice and watch the cranes, geese and the predators and scavengers above them.

notes: The species list comes from GBIF occurrence records inside a circle around the park, so it can include nearby areas. Feeding links come from GloBI records and the sources listed where they state them; others are general ecology and are illustrative.

nodes.desc: A tall wetland grass that forms dense stands along rivers and marshes. Water deer shelter in tall reeds, and red-crowned cranes nest in tall-grass wetlands.
A dominant oak of Korean mountain forests whose acorns feed many animals, from rodents to gorals.
An omnivore that eats plants, small animals and carrion. GloBI records show it eating field mice, geese and snakes near the zone.
A small rodent of fields and grassland that eats seeds and grain, and is food for many predators.
An omnivorous canid of Korean woods and farmland that eats small animals, plants and carrion.
A small carnivore that hunts mice and hares; GloBI records also list birds and a leopard cat among its prey.
A small wild cat that hunts rodents and other small animals. Wikipedia notes it occasionally ambushes young cranes in South Korea.

nodes.name: Steppes ratsnake
nodes.desc: A non-venomous snake of fields and scrub. GloBI has records of wild boar eating it.
A huge scavenger that feeds mostly on carrion and winters in South Korea. GloBI has a record of it eating water deer.
Wikipedia names this endangered bear among the DMZ animals. It is a mostly plant-eating omnivore that relies on acorns and also takes carrion.
Summer sun and heat drive fast plant growth in the monsoon season.
Summer rains fill the rivers, marshes and paddies on which reeds and rice depend.
Cold winters push cranes and geese south to the open farmland and rivers of the zone.
Nutrients in the soil feed forest, grass and crop growth.

nodes.name: Fungi & bacteria
nodes.desc: Break down dead plants, carcasses and dung and return nutrients to the soil.
